headline: Cloud-led growth continues, margins soften sequentially
summary_short: Jack Henry reported revenue of $636.2M, up 8.7% y/y on organic cloud, card, and payments growth, while diluted EPS of $1.71 rose 12.2% y/y but slipped $0.01 q/q as operating income and net income each pulled back 2-3% sequentially.
summary_long: Revenue rose 8.7% y/y (7.3% organic ex-deconversion) to $636.2M, led by cloud hosting, card, and faster-payments growth. Operating income grew 11.8% y/y as revenue outpaced a 7.8% rise in operating expenses from higher personnel and direct costs. Net income rose 10.6% y/y to $122.9M ($1.71 diluted EPS, +12.2% y/y) despite a higher effective tax rate (22.5% vs 21.7%) as prior-year investment-tax-credit benefits rolled off. Sequentially, EBIT, EBITDA, and net income each fell 1-3% versus a strong prior quarter. Cash fell to $20.6M and long-term debt rose to $90.0M after drawing on the new $1B revolver to fund $284.4M of YTD buybacks and $127.5M of dividends. FY2026 capex guided to $100M-$130M.

drivers.explanation: Organic growth in data processing/hosting (private and public cloud), Jack Henry digital and transaction, card, and faster-payments revenue lines; ex-deconversion growth was 7.3% y/y.
Higher personnel costs from a trailing-twelve-month headcount increase, higher direct costs tracking revenue growth, and increased intangible amortization.
Organic revenue growth outpaced a 7.8% rise in operating expenses, tempered by the company's cost-discipline efforts, y/y.
Sequential pullback follows a stronger December-quarter base; the filing gives no specific q/q cause beyond the underlying expense and tax trends discussed for the y/y comparison.
Effective tax rate rose to 22.5% from 21.7% y/y primarily because prior-year investment-tax-credit purchase benefits did not recur, diluting the relative tax-benefit impact this year.
Financing activities used $320.5M YTD — $284.4M for treasury-stock buybacks, $127.5M for dividends, and $270.0M of credit-facility repayments, partially offset by new borrowings.
Company drew on credit facilities during the year to help fund buybacks and dividends; entered a new 5-year $1B revolving credit agreement on March 25, 2026, replacing the prior facility.
